claims.summary: Likely Snags (hypothesis): `first_word_after` (L89, trim L92) `split_whitespace`+`trim_matches` might mishandle complex punctuation, Unicode whitespace, or zero-width chars, fail to identify the relation verb, and strip or retain the marker incorrectly.
claims.disposition: Concern preserved, not domesticated. Complete source + passing regressions show leading format chars (NBSP U+00A0, ZWNBSP U+FEFF, soft hyphen U+00AD, multibyte emoji) are edge-trimmed so the verb is found and marker preserved; an INTERNAL format char is not on a trim edge, so the exact allowlist match fails and the marker fails CLOSED (stripped, never leaked). No incorrect retention path exists. A mid-verb zero-width char travels the identical edge-only-trim code path already pinned by _internal_soft_hyphen (tests.rs L3199-3240).
